review_comments.body: **Warning records grow without limit** `skippedToolWarned` retains every invalid name ever returned, not just the current tool list. A long-lived server returning changing names such as `/resource/1` and `/resource/2` keeps adding entries even after those tools disappear. Only client removal clears them. Add a per-client size or byte limit so repeated discovery cannot grow retained memory indefinitely. **How this was verified:** Names from the upstream `tools/list` response become full map keys, and the only deletion path runs when the client is removed.

**New clients lose warnings** Warning records belong to a reusable name rather than one client instance. Renaming client `A` to `B` leaves `A`'s records behind, so a newly added client named `A` can lose its first warnings. An in-flight per-call refresh can also insert old records after `RemoveClient` clears them, suppressing warnings when that name is added again. Keep the warning set with the client instance and pass that set into discovery, so old work cannot affect a replacement client. **Knowledge Base Used:** [MCP tools and client lifecycle](https://app.greptile.com/maxim-ai/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/maximhq/bifrost/-/docs/mcp-tools-and-client-lifecycle.md)

**Related tests are split** `AGENTS.md` requires tests to go in an existing related test file, not a new file for each fix. Move this test and its helpers into `refreshtools_test.go`, which already covers `RefreshClientTools` and supplies `newRefreshConfig`. This keeps discovery tests together. The repository requirement must be satisfied before merging. **File Used:** `AGENTS.md` ([source](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/98263e1d531b4a9029386d2e6d5c0ae243cce621/AGENTS.md)) Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

**Migrate skipped-tool warning records when a client is renamed.** `UpdateClient` can rename an existing client without replacing its runtime state. The warning record remains keyed by the old name. After the rename, retrieval uses the new name, so the renamed client warns once again. If that client is removed, cleanup deletes only records under the new name. A later client reusing the old name can therefore suppress its first warning. This affects warning visibility only. Skipped tools remain reported to plugins. Key records by stable client identity, or migrate them during rename, and clear all records when the client is removed.

**Bound the warning records.** Each invalid tool name is retained until the client is removed. Tool synchronization runs every 10 minutes by default, but a per-client interval of one second is allowed. A configured MCP server that returns changing invalid names can therefore grow this map across syncs, even after earlier tools disappear. The per-entry memory cost is small, so major memory exhaustion is not justified. Treat this as a minor stability concern. Bound the per-client records and define warning behavior when the bound is reached.

Good point. Each tool sync now prunes the client's warning records down to the invalid tools that sync returned (`pruneSkippedToolWarnings` in `retrieveExternalToolsDetailed`), so names that come and go no longer accumulate; the record for a client is bounded by the invalid tools it currently lists. Covered by `TestToolSync_SkippedToolWarningsAreBoundedAndFollowRename`.

Rename: `UpdateClient` now drops the records kept under the old name when the client name changes, so a client later added under that name warns again (tested in `TestToolSync_SkippedToolWarningsAreBoundedAndFollowRename`).

In-flight refresh vs `RemoveClient`: left as is, deliberately. The only effect is that one first warning for a re-added client of the same name could be suppressed, and the next sync prunes stale entries anyway. Moving the set onto the client instance would mean changing the `runListToolsWithHooks` / `retrieveExternalToolsDetailed` signatures, which seems out of proportion for a log-level fix. Happy to do it in this PR if you prefer.
Done: the test and its helpers moved into `core/mcp/refreshtools_test.go` next to the other `RefreshClientTools` tests, and `skippedtoolwarn_test.go` is gone.

Both addressed in the follow-up commit:
- Rename: `UpdateClient` forgets the old name's records when the client is renamed; removal already cleared them.
- Bound: each sync prunes the client's records to the invalid tools it currently lists, so changing names cannot grow the map across syncs. With that, the per-client record is at most one entry per invalid tool the server lists right now, so a separate size cap with a limit warning did not seem necessary.

This follow-up was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent (Claude).

Thanks—the rename cleanup addresses the stale-name case I called out. I’m okay leaving the in-flight refresh race as-is: it can cause a replacement client’s first warning for the same invalid tool to be logged at debug instead, but it doesn’t affect discovery or tool behavior. Given that limited, explicitly accepted tradeoff, I don’t think moving the set onto each client instance is necessary for this log-level fix.
